Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Yesterday was the fifth anniversary of the launching of the Iraq War, and ABC’s Martha Raddatz interviewed Vice-President Cheney. Here is a brief but telling excerpt: 

Raddatz: “Two-thirds of Americans say it’s not worth fighting, and they’re looking at the value gain versus the cost in American lives, certainly, and Iraqi lives.” 

Cheney: “So?” 

Raddatz:” So — you don’t care what the American people think”? 

Cheney: “No, I think you cannot be blown off course by the fluctuations in the public opinion polls.” 

In most surveys more than two-thirds of Americans say they are favor medical access to cannabis, but we are not likely to hear anyone from ABC ask such a question about that, but we are regularly told that the opinion of the people doesn’t count there either. From 2002, see 

Democracy, Cannabis and the Drug Czar. Arrests Remain Close to Record Levels. Support for Medical Cannabis Now Up to 80%. And 34% Favor Full Legalization. We Are Winning, But The People Are Suffering. 

and from 2003, see 

California Democrats Discover Democracy, State Democratic Council Endorses Medical Marijuana. Online Poll of Doctors Shows 76% In Favor. If The People Will Lead, The Leaders Will Follow. 

The Bee article explained that the Supervisors ignored the pleas of 30 patients, and “Tuesday's 3-2 vote was instead in step with the position of Sacramento County's law enforcement officials that implementing the program would invite residents to violate federal law…. Sheriff John McGinness and District Attorney Jan Scully argued against the program…. 

He added that issuing cards would encourage pot use. "We have a conflict," he said. "We are talking about a behavior that is illegal by federal law." 

The Sheriff and the DA also ignored the state’s constitution. 

See 

California Constitution Specifically Prohibits State Officials From Using Federal Laws As An Excuse For Not Enforcing State Laws Like Prop 215 Without A Court Ruling. Great Orange County Register Editorial. 

and 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for December 6, 2007 – The Drug War Is Racist; Colorado and California police Have to Follow State NOT Federal Laws; Hemp Still Scares Narks. 

and 

The Crisis in Democracy, Prohibitionism And The Police Fiasco. Why Will It Work In Iraq, If It Does Not Work In DEAland? 

They also ignored the fact that all but 18 of the state’s 58 counties have adopted the state card program, but the card’s are not mandatory and all they intended to do is to keep the patients from being arrested under state law. They do not protect patients from federal law enforcement or other unnatural disasters. 

However, the Feds are generally more inhibited in their depredations in areas in which the local law enforcement is not run by Quisling collaborators, as it is in Sacramento and San Diego. 

See 

Old Lies in A New Package. Drug Czar’s “2008 National Drug Control Strategy” Again Demonstrates the Drug War Is Really A War on Cannabis Users. Part One "Potency"

In the Bay Area the US Attorney recently indicated the futility of raiding dispensaries.

See 

US Attorney for Northern California Makes Nice, Maybe; LA Counterpart Talks Tough. Berkeley Better Than Oakland? One Nation Under A Bush? 

Then yesterday, in what was really just a terrible coincidence in timing, but not in substance, “U.S. District Judge Frank C. Damrell Jr. said federal law left him with no choice but to impose on both Dr. Marion "Mollie" Fry and attorney Dale Schafer the mandatory minimum sentence.” 

Again, as the Bee reported, Fry and Schafer “were sentenced… in Sacramento federal court to five years in prison for conspiring to grow and distribute marijuana.” 

Then saying, “It is a sad day, a terrible day."— the judge allowed them to remain free on bail until their appeals have been decided. He even “told Fry and Schafer they're martyrs, but he questioned whether their cause merited such a sacrifice, especially since they have children at home and help care for a grandchild,” and were it left up to him, “the punishment would be less. " 

A Federal judge is more sympathetic than the Sacramento DA and Sheriff! 

The Bee article is also very sympathetic in its tone and observed, “The couple went from personal marijuana use – radical breast cancer surgery in Fry's case, severe back pain and a dangerous form of hemophilia for Schafer – to supplying the drug to people who came to them with various ailments.”

They insisted they didn't expect trouble from federal narcotics agents because they were not selling the drug, they were careful to comply with California's Compassionate Use Act, and what they were doing was encouraged by El Dorado County narcotics officers. 

In a very odd twist, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Lawrence Brown confirmed that Fry was offered straight probation in return for a plea, which she did not accept, “because the deal would have been based in part on her serious mental health problems, and she was afraid of the impact that might have on the state Medical Board, which licenses and regulates physicians.” 

Now, let’s get this straight, a mother/grandmother who has survived breast cancer and – not surprisingly – has “serious mental health problems” was prosecuted for “conspiring” to help sick and dying people and will now have to spend five years in a federal prison. Okay, so who really has “serious mental health problems”??? 

It is clear that the judge is also sympathetic to the medical use of cannabis, but there is also enormous irony in his statement to the defendants: "At some point, it seems to me, you lost control of your lives. You let your passion for this drug and its salutary effects cloud your judgment.” 

Yes, they lost control of their lives when they thought they lived in a free country, in a state where they were protected by the law, and their compassion certainly clouded their judgment. 

As for the New Orleans reference, remember that this took place in Sacramento, the capital of the “sovereign” state of California, where the local law enforcement defers to the Federal government. If one looks at a map, Sacramento is more or less in the middle of the state, but it is actually just a few feet above sea level, surrounded by two rives and protected by aging levies. Sound familiar? 

Well, it gets worse. The Feds won’t pay for levy repairs and the state has severe budget problems – in part because it spends billions every year on its huge prison system. Yes, if the levies break, another small city would flood, sad, but so what? 

So, consider this excerpt from a PBS NewsHour Report from December 22, 2005: 

“You could bankrupt this state if you had a major levee failure in one of the large metropolitan areas… 

The area most at risk is California's central valley, along the Sacramento and San Joaquin Rivers, which carry huge quantities of water from the Sierra Nevada Mountains to San Francisco Bay. 

Cities built behind the valley's thousands of miles of levees are especially vulnerable, and so is the delta. The delta is a large, mostly below-sea-level region where water from the two rivers courses through hundreds of channels toward the bay past primitively constructed dirt levees built a century ago.

Freshwater from the delta supplies 23 million people in urban southern California and the bay area, and irrigates some of the most productive farmland in the world. If levees were to break, saltwater would be sucked into the delta from San Francisco Bay, ruining the water quality and halting the flow of water south. 

This is the fifth-largest economy in the world, and what happens to this economy affects the world. So that's why you worry about it at the highest levels, the disruption of water supply… And that would be extended outages of water export for the state and its economy, maybe for a very long time. You'd be looking at maybe $30 to $40 billion.” 

The Supervisors of Sacramento County, where half of the city's current home sales involve bank-owned property, are willing to spend money on arresting sick and dying Californians, and the State government watches from a few blocks away, but they cannot afford to fix the  levies that protect the Capital, and the state’s water supply. And the Federal government has the authority and resources to prosecute and imprison a couple with serious medical problems, but it is unwilling to fund the repair of the levies that protect the water supply of the most important economy in the country. 

Yes, I have the greatest sympathy for Schafer and Fry, but this tragedy goes far, far beyond this couple.

441 1/2 E. 16th St., 4427 1/2 Crenshaw, 1321 E. Compton, 14102 S. Vermont, and have completed a raid at 467 N. Western.
